sentences.text: This application under Section 430(1) of the Bharathiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023, has been filed seeking suspension of sentence of the applicant/accused in S.C.No.2041/2022 on the file of the Court of Session, Kollam.

He has been found guilty for the offences punishable under Sections 450,
354(B) and 376(3) IPC, Section 4(2) read with Section 3(a) of the PoCSO Act.
He has been sentenced to varying terms of imprisonment for the aforesaid offences.
The sentences have been directed to run concurrently.
The maximum period of imprisonment the applicant/accused will have to undergo is 20 years.

Set off has been allowed under Section 428 of Cr.P.C.
2.
It is submitted by the learned counsel for the in and applicant/accused that he was only 18 years at the time of the incident.

My attention is also drawn to paragraph no.11 of the impugned judgment,
a reading of which makes
it clear that PW1, the victim, and the applicant/accused were in a relationship
. No force, threat or coercion was exercised by the applicant/accused and taking into account the facts and circumstances of the case, the sentence may be suspended, goes the argument.

3. The learned public prosecutor objects to the application on the ground that even if it was a consensual relationship, PW1 being a minor, the consent given is immaterial and that no exceptional circumstances are made out to suspend the sentence.

4. Heard both sides.
5.
On going through the impugned judgment, I find that that applicant/accused was only 18 years at the time of the incident.
A reading of paragraph no.11 would show that the relationship was consensual.
However, PW1 being a minor, the in and consent given is 'no consent' in the eye of law.
There is only one incident on the basis of which the crime has been registered.
It is submitted by the learned public prosecutor on instructions that the applicant/accused has no criminal antecedents.
The appeal is of the year 2024 and hence there is no possibility of the appeal being taken in the near future.
